3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: It was early in the morning. Lucita and I were about to depart for a royal visit to Terador Air Force Base when I got an urgent summons from Hugo.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: I walked through the council chamber doors to find my uncle and my foreign affairs councilor waiting for me.

5.speaker: Player_Romus
5.text: "Mr. Esquibel, Your Grace. To what do I owe this interruption?"

7.speaker: Player_Romus
7.text: "I hope this is quick, gentlemen. Duchess Azaro and I are on a tight schedule."

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: The two men glanced at each other.

9.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
9.text: "Your Majesty... we have received the results from the joint investigation into the Palesian border incident."

10.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
10.text: "Quite simply, our earlier hypotheses that the attack was incited by Pales or staged by a third party were not borne out."

11.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
11.text: "Instead, all evidence seemed to indicate an inside job, one masterminded by..."

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: He took a deep breath. He couldn't bring himself to go on.

14.speaker: Player_Romus
14.text: "Come on, Mr. Esquibel. If there's a traitor in our midst, I need to know who it is."

16.speaker: Hugo Toras
16.text: "The named culprit was Lucita Azaro, Your Majesty."

18.speaker: Player_Romus
18.text: "What?! They'll pay for soiling the name of a capable councilor and esteemed noblewoman."

19.speaker: Player_Romus
19.text: "The Azaros have been working against me this whole time?"

20.speaker: Player_Romus
20.text: "I know Duchess Azaro well. She'd never do a thing like that."

25.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
25.text: "I'd like to believe the same. But you have to consider the possibility that the Duchess entered into your confidence precisely so that you'd take her side in the case of such an incident."

27.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
27.text: "We don't know the precise details. The Duchess could have been acting in cooperation with her house, or alone."

28.speaker: Hugo Toras
28.text: "That was my first thought as well. I don't believe Duchess Azaro would commit such an act."

29.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
29.text: "I am unsure what to think. Honestly, this investigation has muddied more waters than it has cleared."

31.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
31.text: "The report they sent seems to heavily indicate Duchess Azaro's involvement in what happened."

32.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
32.text: "The investigators secured a testimony from the commanding officer at the Fort Ales garrison. Apparently he told his men to fire on the Palesians on Duchess Azaro's orders."

33.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
33.text: "He was then coerced into altering the reports of the incident to suggest that was Pales who shot first."

34.speaker: Player_Romus
34.text: "Lucita would have to be an idiot to think that she could get away with that."

35.speaker: Player_Romus
35.text: "And we trust this officer? What if he's the one who organized everything?"

36.speaker: Player_Romus
36.text: "I always did suspect Duchess Azaro of being disingenuous in her pacifism."

37.speaker: Player_Romus
37.text: "How could she do this while my daughter was still in Pales? She must have known there was a risk Vina would get caught up in it."

38.speaker: Hugo Toras
38.text: "It does seem rather obvious for a military officer of her caliber."

39.speaker: Hugo Toras
39.text: "The man's record is spotless. But we cannot rule out that possibility."

40.speaker: Hugo Toras
40.text: "If she was suspicious of the Palesians, it was for a reason."

44.speaker: Hugo Toras
44.text: "Yes. She is not her father's daughter."

45.speaker: Player_Romus
45.text: "Why would she plan such a thing? She always cautioned me to be diplomatic with the Grand Duchy."

47.speaker: Hugo Toras
47.text: "To me, these results don't add up. It is far more likely that Pales -- or someone else -- is trying to paint Rizia as an aggressor to sabotage our gas deal.

48.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
48.text: "I agree that this is far from a clear-cut case. Lespia had officials on the investigation committee, after all."

49.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
49.text: "May I remind you of her suggestion to send a naval blockade to Aureus? Had we agreed to that, we would be in far more trouble than we are right now."

50.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
50.text: "She may have been counting on Rizia to invade Pales first and ask questions later."

51.speaker: Hugo Toras
51.text: "Which gives more credence to the theory that the Duchess is innocent."

52.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
52.text: "Or acting under extreme pressure from her own family."

53.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
53.text: "But we still have a chance to salvage our gas deal and our diplomatic relationship with Pales. We just have to ensure the blame for the border attack falls fully on Duchess Azaro's shoulders, not ours."

54.speaker: Player_Romus
54.text: "Are you suggesting we turn in a woman who may be innocent just to avoid conflict?"

55.speaker: Player_Romus
55.text: "It's obvious to me that Lespia played a role. Most likely hoping that Pales would use the investigation results as grounds to cancel our gas deal."

56.speaker: Player_Romus
56.text: "Pales wants us to take our best military strategist off the chessboard. Rather suspicious, that."

57.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
57.text: "But if that's true, then denying Duchess Azaro's involvement is playing right into Lespia's hands."

58.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
58.text: "I don't see another way out of it, unfortunately."

59.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
59.text: "Arrest Duchess Azaro now, and we can claim the incident was the work of a sole actor."

60.speaker: Player_Romus
60.text: "Reinhart demanded reparations, and I paid them. Now he wants our best military strategist?"

64.speaker: Hugo Toras
64.text: "It could well be the case that Pales and Lespia were in cahoots all along. They may never have truly intended to sell us the gas field."

65.speaker: Hugo Toras
65.text: "Only if Pales is serious about honoring the terms of our deal. Which it may not be."

66.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
66.text: "Pales promised to honor the deal if Rizia's name was cleared. If we name Duchess Azaro as the sole actor responsible for the incident, Duke Reinhart will have to go through with the sale."

67.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
67.text: "Defend her, on the other hand, and Pales as well as the entire international community will believe the Rizian government was behind the border operation."

68.speaker: Player_Romus
68.text: "That's great news. The Azaro traitor will face justice, and our deal can proceed as planned."

69.speaker: Hugo Toras
69.text: "If she is innocent -- or even if she is not -- the fallout from House Azaro will be disastrous."

70.speaker: Laurento Esquibel
70.text: "Not as disastrous as that from the international community should we fail to acknowledge the results of the investigation."

71.speaker: Narrator
71.text: An aide rushed into the chambers with the blue telephone. Duke Reinhart was calling.

72.speaker: Narrator
72.text: Hugo and Laurento stayed silent in the background as I picked up the receiver.

73.speaker: Axel Reinhart
73.text: "King Romus. I'm assuming you received the same report that I did?"

74.speaker: Player_Romus
74.text: "I received it. I'm still deciding what to make of it."

75.speaker: Player_Romus
75.text: "Yes. I can't believe my own war councilor would betray me like that."

76.speaker: Player_Romus
76.text: "Tell me, Your Grace. Did Pales or Lespia have a hand in these investigation results?"

77.speaker: Player_Romus
77.text: "I'm hoping I didn't. Because this one is blaming an innocent woman for what happened."

78.speaker: Axel Reinhart
78.text: "Were you really so surprised, Your Majesty?"

79.speaker: Axel Reinhart
79.text: "What is there to decide, Your Majesty?"

80.speaker: Axel Reinhart
80.text: "Are you trying to deflect the blame, Your Majesty?"

81.speaker: Narrator
81.text: The volume of his voice rose.

82.speaker: Axel Reinhart
82.text: "Your war councilor's father got us into this entanglement to begin with. With this gas deal, you were about to acknowledge my country's sovereignty and take the possibility of a second invasion completely off the table. Obviously she wouldn't stand for that."

84.speaker: Player_Romus
84.text: "Think about it for a second. Isn't it more likely that Lespia was behind the incident?"

88.speaker: Axel Reinhart
88.text: "Lespia didn't kill my soldiers. That was all Rizia's doing."

89.speaker: Player_Romus
89.text: "Our fathers do not determine our destiny."

90.speaker: Axel Reinhart
90.text: "Are you suggesting we accuse an ATO member state of falsifying investigation results?"

91.speaker: Player_Romus
91.text: "Whatever she did, she acted alone. Neither I nor my other councilors had any knowledge of it."

92.speaker: Player_Romus
92.text: "Admit it. You don't *want* Rizia to acknowledge Palesian sovereignty. It's far more convenient for you to play the victim."

93.speaker: Axel Reinhart
93.text: "Please, Your Majesty. Make this easy for us both."

94.speaker: Axel Reinhart
94.text: "Arrest the Azaro woman, and we can get on with this deal and our lives."

96.speaker: Axel Reinhart
96.text: "In this case, they do. The evidence is right in front of our faces."

98.speaker: Player_Romus
98.text: "I still have my suspicions about the legitimacy of these findings. But for the sake of lasting peace between our nations, Duchess Azaro will face justice."

99.speaker: Player_Romus
99.text: "Rest assured that my war councilor will be punished for her treasonous act. I will personally make sure she is shown no mercy."

100.speaker: Player_Romus
100.text: "I'm sorry, Your Grace, but I cannot acknowledge the investigation results. I fully believe that my councilor is innocent."

101.speaker: Player_Romus
101.text: "No. Your Grand Duchy has double-crossed me for the last time. I don't know what scheme you're trying to pull, but I won't go along with it."

102.speaker: Narrator
102.text: There was a long silence on the other end. Laurento and Hugo sat by with bated breath as I awaited the Duke's response.

103.speaker: Axel Reinhart
103.text: "I am sorry you see it that way, Your Majesty."

104.speaker: Axel Reinhart
104.text: "You have left me with no choice. The Aureus deal is off."

106.speaker: Axel Reinhart
106.text: "The gas pipeline from the field to Rizia will be dismantled at once. All Rizian vessels in the vicinity will be ordered to leave, and Rizian access to the field will be blocked indefinitely."

107.speaker: Player_Romus
107.text: "This was your plan all along, wasn't it? Take our money, then steal back your gas field."

108.speaker: Player_Romus
108.text: "Who will buy the exploration rights from you, then? Lespia?"

109.speaker: Narrator
109.text: There was a long silence on the other end. Laurento and Hugo sat by with bated breath as I awaited the Duke's response.

111.speaker: Axel Reinhart
111.text: "I'm glad we were able to resolve this little hiccup in a civil manner."

112.speaker: Player_Romus
112.text: "Arresting the heir to one of Rizia's most important noble families is far from a 'little hiccup', Duke Reinhart. I hope you appreciate that."

114.speaker: Player_Romus
114.text: "So am I. I am certain this unpleasant affair won't even make it into the history books."

118.speaker: Player_Romus
118.text: "Now, will you send my daughter back home?"

119.speaker: Axel Reinhart
119.text: "Yes, yes, of course. Though I confess I've grown rather fond of having her around."

120.speaker: Player_Romus
120.text: "So our gas deal is still on? Exactly as before?"

122.speaker: Axel Reinhart
122.text: "It is nothing compared to the magnitude of what we are about to accomplish."

127.speaker: Player_Romus
127.text: "Please, Your Grace. Surely we can still reach some sort of compromise?"

128.speaker: Axel Reinhart
128.text: "Arresting Duchess Azaro *was* the compromise, I'm afraid."

129.speaker: Axel Reinhart
129.text: "Assuming you respect our decision to cancel our deal, I shall send her back immediately."

130.speaker: Axel Reinhart
130.text: "Although I confess I've grown rather fond of having her around."

134.speaker: Axel Reinhart
134.text: "Needless to say, Princess Vina shall be returned home at once. Although I confess I've grown rather fond of having her around."

135.speaker: Axel Reinhart
135.text: "The fact that you could even think that is proof your kingdom never wanted to reconcile with Pales in the first place."

140.speaker: Axel Reinhart
140.text: "I will send your daughter back immediately, assuming you respect our decision to cancel the deal."

142.speaker: Player_Romus
142.text: "No. You signed the rights to the Aureus field over to Rizia. If we must take it by force, we will." [Declare War]

143.speaker: Player_Romus
143.text: "Listen here, you brat. Do you know what happens when you try to back a bull into a corner? It charges." [Declare War]

147.speaker: Narrator
147.text: Laurento looked stricken. Hugo's expression had turned determined.

148.speaker: Player_Romus
148.text: "Yes. We will forfeit our right to the field."

149.speaker: Player_Romus
149.text: "You are making a mistake. But I will not challenge your decision."

151.speaker: Axel Reinhart
151.text: "I suppose it was always going to come to this."

152.speaker: Axel Reinhart
152.text: "We defended ourselves against Rizia once. We are ready to do so again."

156.speaker: Axel Reinhart
156.text: "And this time, we have a very comely young bargaining chip."

159.speaker: Narrator
159.text: I looked at the clock. It was time for our visit to Terador.

161.speaker: Axel Reinhart
161.text: "Of course, I will make sure every nation in Merkopa is aware that Rizia sheltered a known criminal."

162.speaker: Axel Reinhart
162.text: "But other than that... no hard feelings, Your Majesty."

166.speaker: Axel Reinhart
166.text: "Thank you for seeing reason, Your Majesty."

167.speaker: Narrator
167.text: Laurento let out a long exhale of relief. Hugo's expression didn't change.

168.speaker: Player_Romus
168.text: "We'll speak soon. For now, I have an arrest to make."

169.speaker: Player_Romus
169.text: "I'll see you at the deal signing."

172.speaker: Narrator
172.text: Laurento, Hugo and I looked at each other. Nobody spoke for a moment.

173.speaker: Hugo Toras
173.text: "Well. As the Rizia Imperii police are under Ms. Azaro's command, I'll order the Golden Guard to detain the Duchess until a proper arrest can be made."

174.speaker: Player_Romus
174.text: "Tell them to tell her I'm sorry."

175.speaker: Player_Romus
175.text: "Tell them to use as much force as they need to."

176.speaker: Player_Romus
176.text: "I control the Golden Guard. I will give the orders."

181.speaker: Narrator
181.text: He looked at me with sorrow in his eyes.

185.speaker: Narrator
185.text: I called Titus in and told him he had work to do.

192.speaker: Narrator
192.text: I thought about the night Lucita and I had spent in Qalus and all the moments we'd stolen since then. Images of what could have been flashed through my mind.

193.speaker: Narrator
193.text: I thought about the way Lucita had looked at me back in Qalus. I had told her I'd take her on a date someday. We'd never get that chance now.

194.speaker: Narrator
194.text: I thought about the night Lucita and I had spent in Qalus and all the moments we'd stolen since then. Images of what could have been flashed through my mind.

195.speaker: Narrator
195.text: I thought about the way Lucita had looked at me back in Qalus. I had told her I'd take her on a date someday. We'd never get that chance now.

202.speaker: Narrator
202.text: Still lost in my thoughts, I watched as Hugo called Titus into the room and told him he had work to do.

203.speaker: Narrator
203.text: I thought about the conversation I'd had with Lucita in Montaklar. If House Toras and House Azaro ever were truly allied, they weren't now.

225.speaker: Narrator
225.text: As for what role, if any, she had played in my father's death... I would probably never know.

229.speaker: Narrator
229.text: As for what role, if any, she had played in my father's death... I would probably never know.

230.speaker: Narrator
230.text: I thought about the conversation I'd had with Lucita in Montaklar. If House Toras and House Azaro ever were truly allied, they weren't now.
